content: Once prescribed, it is essential to complete the full course of this medication, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects may include swelling, redness, pain, or soreness at the injection site. Rarely, this medication may cause a loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or headache. It is important to remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the potential risks of side effects. In rare cases, this medication may lead to a severe intestinal condition caused by the bacteria Clostridium difficile (C. difficile). This condition can occur during treatment or even weeks to months after treatment has ended. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. This is not an exhaustive list of potential side effects. If you are in the United States or Canada and experience side effects, contact your doctor for medical advice. Before using cefotaxime, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other cephalosporins, penicillins, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Cefotaxime may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. Additionally, this medication can pass into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. It is important to maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs, as well as herbal products, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as Coombs' tests, urine glucose tests, and serum or urine creatinine tests, potentially leading to false results. In the event of an overdose, if the individual has serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition and should not be used for other purposes. While using this product, your doctor may order laboratory or medical tests, such as a complete blood count or kidney function tests, to monitor your progress. If you miss a dose, consult your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. For storage instructions, refer to the product guidelines or consult your pharmacist. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
